Definition: What proportion of businesses does the register cover?
revision_notes: Original sources (CIPA, doingbusiness.co.bw) confirm the Online Business Registration System (OBRS) exists and processes routine applications within 24 hours, but neither gives a coverage percentage. World Bank Enterprise Surveys 2023 country profile provides the missing evidence: 92.2% of firms report having been formally registered when they started operations, which supports the >89% band. Score of 5 confirmed as unchanged.
revised_comments: Botswana's Companies and Intellectual Property Authority (CIPA) operates the Online Business Registration System (OBRS), enabling online company name reservation and incorporation, with routine approvals typically issued within 24 hours. World Bank Enterprise Surveys data for 2023 show that 92.2% of firms report having been formally registered when they began operations, indicating that formal business registration coverage exceeds 89% of the formal business population.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: National population registry exists via DCNR with digital backend (NIS), Omang ID issuance; processes manual but centralized production.
revision_notes: Original sources confirmed and supplemented with a December 2025 IDS/ADRN country report on Botswana's Omang biometric digital-ID system and a July 2023 government statement on the still-in-development electronic Omang card. Evidence shows the Department of Civil and National Registration (DCNR) maintains a centralised National Identification System (NIS)/population database with biometric data (fingerprints, and increasingly facial recognition), linked in real time to civil registration, the electoral roll, the social benefits register and government payroll. However, registration and card production remain a manual, in-person process (around 14 working days turnaround via district/sub-district offices) and a fully electronic, chip-based ID card was still under development as of mid-2023. Score of 4 (Partially deployed) confirmed as unchanged; year updated to reflect the most recent evidence rather than the original 2018 diagnostic.
revised_comments: Botswana's Department of Civil and National Registration (DCNR) maintains a centralised National Identification System (NIS) underpinning the Omang national identity card, which has evolved into a biometric platform incorporating fingerprint and, increasingly, facial recognition data. The NIS is linked in real time to civil registration, the electoral roll, the social benefits register (SOBERS) and government payroll systems, and issues a unique identifier at birth that becomes the citizen's Omang number from age sixteen. Registration and card production nonetheless remain a largely manual, in-person process through district and sub-district offices, with a standard processing time of around fourteen working days, and a fully electronic identity card with advanced digital features remained under development as of 2023. The register is therefore best characterised as partially, rather than fully, digitally deployed.
